blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A company is not only a taxpayer on its own profit. It is also a collector of tax for the government — on VAT it adds to invoices, on income tax it withholds from salaries, and on payments to certain suppliers. In every one of these roles, the company has a legal duty to calculate correctly, to collect correctly, and to hand the money over on time.

Mistakes in these roles are often taken more seriously than mistakes in the company's own tax bill. The reason is simple: when a company miscalculates its own tax, it is hurting itself. When it miscalculates what it is supposed to collect for the government, it is, in a sense, taking someone else's money.

A good finance team keeps these two roles clearly separated in its own head — 'tax we owe' and 'tax we collect' — and treats the second with slightly more care than the first.

items.q: According to the text, in which roles does a company act besides paying tax on its own profit?
options: It collects tax for the government
It only audits its own accounts
It refunds tax to customers
It sets the national tax rates
items.why: "It is also a collector of tax for the government" — VAT, income tax retido, etc.

items.q: What are the three legal duties the text lists for these collecting roles?
options: To estimate, to negotiate and to defer
To report, to audit and to publish
To calculate, to collect and to hand the money over on time
To invoice, to invest and to reconcile
items.why: "calculate correctly… collect correctly… hand the money over on time."

items.q: Why are mistakes in the collecting role treated more seriously?
options: Because they always involve larger amounts
Because the company is mishandling money that belongs to someone else
Because they are harder to detect
Because they damage the company's credit rating
items.why: "it is, in a sense, taking someone else's money" — não é dinheiro da empresa.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The tax a company collects deserves at least as much care as the tax it owes.
An error in withheld income tax is no more serious than an error in corporate tax.
A company can be both a taxpayer and a tax collector at the same time.
Keeping the two roles mentally separate reduces risk.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro defende que o erro no imposto arrecadado é MAIS grave, não igual.

items.q: What does keeping 'tax we owe' and 'tax we collect' separate suggest about good practice?
options: Only the tax the company owes really needs monitoring
The two should be paid from the same account for simplicity
Collected tax should be treated as the company's own reserve
Clarity about whose money it is helps prevent costly errors
items.why: Inferência: separar os papéis na cabeça e no processo é o que protege contra o erro mais grave.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver revisando o processo de imposto sobre a folha com o novo júnior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, so this is the payroll run, and I want to walk you through why we double-check the withholding line before anything else.

Every month we take income tax out of people's salaries. That money is never ours — not for a single day. We hold it, and then we hand it over to the tax office by the deadline. So think of us as a middleman, not an owner.

Now, imagine we get the corporate tax slightly wrong on our own profit. That's a problem, we fix it, we pay a small penalty, and honestly we're only hurting ourselves. But if we under-withhold from a hundred salaries, we've collected less than we owe the government on someone else's behalf. That's a completely different kind of mistake, and the tax office treats it that way.

So the rule I want you to remember is simple. When the number is 'tax we collect', you check it twice. When it's 'tax we owe', once is fine. Same care in the end, maybe — but never less on the collecting side. Clear?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver want to check before anything else in the payroll run?
options: The total salary cost
The corporate tax estimate
The withholding line
The supplier payments
items.why: "we double-check the withholding line before anything else."

items.q: How does Oliver describe the company's relationship to the withheld income tax?
options: As a lender to the government
As an investor holding the money
As a middleman, not an owner
As the rightful owner of the funds
items.why: "That money is never ours… think of us as a middleman, not an owner."

items.q: Why does Oliver say a small corporate tax error is less serious?
options: Because it is never penalised
Because it can always be deferred
Because the tax office ignores small errors
Because the company is only hurting itself
items.why: "we're only hurting ourselves" — o dinheiro é da própria empresa.

items.q: What can we infer about why Oliver stresses the difference so strongly to a junior?
options: He wants the junior to spend less time on corporate tax
He believes corporate tax errors are impossible to fix
He assumes the junior will never touch payroll
He wants to build the habit of extra caution on collected tax from the start
items.why: Inferência: ele ensina uma regra de hábito ('check it twice') para formar o júnior cedo.

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "Same care in the end, maybe — but never less on the collecting side"?
options: Both roles can safely be checked only once
Corporate tax should always be checked more carefully
Care levels do not matter as long as deadlines are met
The collecting side may deserve equal or greater care, never less
items.why: Inferência: ele admite que o cuidado pode ser igual, mas nunca menor no imposto arrecadado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "As a taxpayer, the company files a return on its own profit each year." A taxpayer is…
options: an official who collects tax
a person or company that owes tax to the state
a government tax office
an accountant who prepares tax returns
items.why: Taxpayer = contribuinte: quem deve imposto ao Estado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "On salaries, the employer must ___ the income tax before paying the net amount."
options: waive
refund
invoice
withhold
items.why: To withhold = reter na fonte o imposto antes de pagar o líquido.

items.q: "Filing on time is a legal duty, not a courtesy." A legal duty is…
options: a tax discount offered by the state
an optional best practice
an internal company guideline
an obligation imposed by law
items.why: Legal duty = obrigação legal: imposta por lei, não opcional.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "After collecting the VAT, the firm must ___ to the tax office by the deadline."
options: sign it off
hold it back
write it off
hand it over
items.why: To hand over = entregar o dinheiro arrecadado ao fisco.

items.q: When the company acts as a collector, it…
options: audits other taxpayers
gathers tax on behalf of the government
decides who is exempt from tax
keeps the tax as extra revenue
items.why: Collector = arrecadador: recolhe o imposto em nome do governo, não é seu.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de finanças e impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on the payroll tax filing." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
reject outright
comment informally
postpone indefinitely
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's not put off the VAT payment — the deadline is Friday." To put off means to…
options: cancel completely
split into instalments
pay in advance
delay to a later time
items.why: Put off = adiar, deixar para depois.

items.q: "We under-withheld last quarter, and now we have to make up for the shortfall." To make up for means to…
options: report it to the board
compensate or offset it
ignore it
dispute it in court
items.why: Make up for = compensar, cobrir aquilo que faltou.

items.q: "Whatever we promise the auditor, we have to follow through." To follow through means to…
options: document it poorly
carry it to completion
revise it halfway
delegate it to another team
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A single wrong rate can add up to a large penalty across a hundred salaries." To add up to means to…
options: round down
cancel out
amount to in total
be deducted from
items.why: Add up to = somar, totalizar — pequenos erros que resultam em muito.
